status: five selected source paths traced; original proposals only

findings.mechanic: Talent acquisition, prerequisites and effective scaling
chain: Bulwark category descriptor -> Birther assigns known/locked category and additive mastery
Levelup spends class or generic point only after prerequisite and cap checks
ActorTalents.learnTalent changes raw rank and refreshes passives
getTalentLevel applies temporary raw-rank alterations and category multiplier
Shield Pummel duration and weapon damage consume effective level and Shield Expertise
rules: techs_req1 uses the next raw talent rank: STR12+2*(rank-1) and actor level rank-1. Category known and earlier-category talent-count rules are separate gates.

Bulwark supplies shield-offense mastery offset0.3. Birther stores that offset and effective mastery adds1. Other selected descriptors can also contribute; this is not an assertion that every possible actor has exactly1.3.
Raw rank, additive equipment/effect rank and category mastery are separate. An unlearned talent remains zero: alterTalentLevelRaw is only applied to positive raw rank.
Pummel duration uses diminishing returns then floors. Weapon multiplier uses base+(high-base)*sqrt((effectiveRank+effectiveShieldExpertise/2)/5). Nominal high parameters are not hard caps.
The ordinary level-up UI caps points, including extra caps above level50 or explicit talent cap bonuses. Forced learn calls intentionally bypass ordinary prerequisites.
findings.exception: Insufficient stat/level/category/dependency or available points stops ordinary learning. Forced birth/item/escort grants use a different acquisition path and must not be interpreted as ordinary training eligibility.
findings.inference: The useful design separation is owned learning versus currently enhanced execution. YAIR already separates observed/understood/owned proficiency and functional mastery; no second rank system is justified.

findings.mechanic: Legal use, resource costs, cooldowns and effect lifecycle
chain: useTalent checks cooldown -> preUseTalent checks body/resource/custom restrictions
Pummel validates equipped shield and projectable target -> two shield attacks
Second hit -> stun immunity -> setEffect physical-save/duration hook
STUNNED adds temporary attributes -> damage and actBase consume them
timedEffects expires -> removeEffect calls deactivate and removes attributes
rules: Pummel declares base stamina8/cooldown6/range1. Pre/post resource code adjusts real cost; these are not guaranteed final costs for every actor.

No shield or missing/unprojectable target returns failure. postUseTalent exits on falsy result, before normal energy/resource spending and cooldown start. A legal completed attack spends even if the second blow misses or the effect is resisted. Other talents may have explicit failed-attempt penalties, so this is not a universal free-failure claim.
Pummel checks canBe(stun), then setEffect calls a distinct physical-save hook that may reject the effect or shorten its duration. Immunity and save are different mechanisms.

STUNNED halves outgoing projected damage, slows movement, puts up to three eligible activated talents on cooldown, and adds half_talents_cooldown. Executable actBase code decrements cooldowns by0.5 rather than1; the effect inline comment saying cooldown does not decrease is stale.
Effect expiry removes the temporary movement/stun/half-cooldown modifiers. It does not rewind damage dealt or restore prior cooldown values.

Shield Wall is a sustain with stamina reservation30, armor/block/control-resistance effects and Block cooldown reduction. The generic sustain path lowers resource maximum, tracks applied costs, and restores maximum/deactivates effects on release. Reservation, one-time action payment and ongoing resource drain are distinct fields.
findings.exception: Cooldown/resource/equipment failure blocks normal use; a second-hit miss/immunity/save rejection yields no stun while the legal action still completes. Release and effect expiry remove future modifiers without undoing spent effort. Shield Wall can be deactivated even when activation custom checks would fail.
findings.inference: Named status effects need real consumers and cleanup. YAIR already has a paid four-minute hook-cooling condition, immunity predicates, power readyAt and defensive windows. Copying the whole stun package would be redundant and poor idle UX; a finite maintained guard is a more distinct proposal.

findings.mechanic: Contextual actor AI and bounded fallback
chain: Elven elite warrior declares tactical AI, equipped shield and Pummel
Engine doAI -> ToME runAI, transition-enabled tactical redirection
Candidate legality/target/resource/range filters -> resolved tactics
Current wants/speed/other actions -> score and choice
useTalent rechecks action -> failed candidate score zero -> bounded retry -> maintenance/movement
rules: ActorAI source initializes ai_transition=true. A tactical actor such as the elven elite warrior therefore routes to improved_tactical under that setting. No runtime configuration was inspected; simple AI actors are not all tactical actors.

Pummel tactical ATTACK1 and DISABLE.stun3 are usefulness inputs, not deterministic priority or guaranteed selection. Candidate admission checks no_npc_use, cooldown, preUseTalent(fake), target range and custom AI checks.

Resolved tactics are multiplied by current wants; speed and level adjustments participate in scoring. Execution calls the same useTalent path. Failed candidate score is zeroed and selection repeats until no useful score, energy used or bounded attempt limit.
If no energy was used, outer AI can perform specified maintenance or safe/approach/flee movement. Eligibility is independent from tactical desirability.
findings.exception: Missing shield/target/range, cooldown or current resource excludes Pummel. A legal but resisted stun is an effect outcome, not an AI execution failure. This review makes no claim of optimal decisions or real use frequencies.
findings.inference: Current YAIR already implements fixed-kit contextual rush/hook/guard/jab selection, legal fallback and revalidation. Reuse that owner for any new guard/material consumers; neither a general utility-AI engine nor a new NPC scaling system is proposed.

findings.mechanic: Quest aftermath, focused progression rewards and separate unlock lifetimes
chain: Escort quest grant -> actor and reachable portal -> escort movement/combat AI
Arrival sets DONE -> reward choice -> selected party member gets specific stat/talent/category state
Failure sets FAILED -> cleanup plus attributed fate and achievement progress
Player-mode partial achievement lives on main actor; completed accolade goes to module profile
Fallen separately requires profile unlock plus current-actor heinous-act predicate
rules: Escort spawns with linked quest, level-matched actor and an eligible distant portal. Spawn/portal failure returns true from on_grant; Quest.init sets do_not_gain and ActorQuest does not register it.

Portal completion opens a selectable reward chat. Individual talent reward may set mastery1 if category unknown, then force-learns that talent. It does NOT call learnTalentType. Category reward calls learnTalentType(tt,false), storing an untrained category that later needs category learning. Specific method, school access and effective mastery are distinct.

Run actor/quest reward state differs from registerEscorts fate counts written through saveModuleProfile. Player-mode partial achievement counts are actor.achievement_data; completed global records use profile achievement output.

Escort saved/lost thresholds9 and player-attributed killed threshold6 are displayed achievements. Fallen heinous-act eligibility reads current-actor killed-escort progress greater than0, so first qualifying event can satisfy that one prerequisite without awarding the six-event accolade.

Fallen also checks profile.mod.allow_build.paladin_fallen and Sun Paladin subclass/Magic25. An inspected end-chat Aeryn-sacrifice path for a Sun Paladin calls Game.setAllowedBuild, which records allow_build in the profile. Meeting the escort-act predicate alone does not grant evolution or future-character policy.
findings.exception: Escort death distinguishes player-attributed betrayal from other loss, removes matching actors and supplies no success reward. Unknown category is not immediately trained; a qualifying local deed cannot bypass remaining profile/class/stat/evolution requirements. Neither source reading nor profile call sites prove save/online durability timing.

findings.inference: An earned focused lesson versus a stocked object reward is a useful local addition. YAIR already has retained feats and one prestige; no account, new-start or generic trophy-driven power system is proposed.

findings.mechanic: Material/ego generation, equipped function and actual damage consumers
chain: Base shield material/generation/equip requirements -> resolved modifier chance
Natural sequential ego attempts -> eligible rarity/level sampling -> material-aware stat merge
Actor wear adds modifiers and item-granted Block -> takeoff reverses own grants
Pummel reads current shield special_combat for attacks
Block reads actual block value -> timed BLOCKING -> damage projector reduces incoming damage
rules: Five base shields have distinct material_level1-5, generation level bands, STR gates11/16/24/35/48, attack payload and block payload. Material level is not the same field as drop level or equip eligibility.

Prefix/suffix chances resolve through mbonus(40,5); they are not fixed40%. Natural ego generation picks an unattempted type and percent-rolls it. Only success advances to another type; first failure terminates the loop, so a later type may never be attempted.

Ego eligibility uses level_range/rarity; material-aware values use effective_ego_material_level or material_level plus current generation level. The reinforced example modifies special_combat.block and independently equipped armor. No actual sampled shield or drop frequency was tested.

hasShield reads real equipped combat records and rejects disarmed actors. onWear/onTakeoff apply/retract temporary values and item talent grants. Grant counts and surplus are per talent, not a source-specific rank ledger.

learnItemTalent executable code assigns an initial cooldown if none exists and preserves an existing cooldown. The nearby comment saying newly learned talents do not start on cooldown conflicts with code and is not used as a rule.

Block builds a two-turn effect from live combatShieldBlock. The damage projector calls do_block for positive damage. The effect returns unchanged damage for self-hit or unsupported type; eligible damage is reduced by actual block power and can feed shield hooks/counterstrike. Taking off an item removes that item grant; neither equipment nor its grant permanently teaches all shield techniques.

The C rng_percent binding reads an integer percent and returns rand_div(100)<threshold. Its registered percent function is called by the Lua immunity/ego checks. Fractional Lua percent inputs are converted to int here. RNG seeding/replay and all distributions are outside this review.
findings.exception: No equipped valid shield/disarmed actor blocks shield techniques. Natural ego roll failure can stop later attempts. Block rejects unsupported/self damage; changed equipment removes future supported function, while spent cooldown/effort is not a free reusable item bonus.

findings.inference: YAIR already has quality/components/rarity and real equipped gear. The specific gap is current sluice field-frame keys projecting one fixed profile, not a missing item/material engine. Two authored material fits are a smaller transfer than procedural ego infrastructure.
